cards.title: Filename convention (so this panel can be maintained)
cards.content:
```text latest_intrusion_<cam>.jpg
    <cam> = doorbell | hallway | waiting_room            (entry cameras)
            control_room_interior | control_room_exit    (control room)
``` Written by `script.snapshot_entry_cameras` and `script.snapshot_control_room_cameras` when they are called with `event_name: intrusion`, which is exactly what `script.phoenix_intrusion_initial_response` does as its FIRST step - before the lights and siren give the intruder a reason to move.
Longer history is written to `/config/www/snapshots/history/<timestamp>_intrusion_<cam>.jpg` and purged after 25 days by `shell_command.purge_old_snapshots`. **This panel could not be built over that history directory**: this host has no read access to `/config` (probed 2026-09-16 - `/config` does not exist here), and Home Assistant's `/local/` static mount does not expose directory listings, so the history files cannot be enumerated by filename. See docs/DASHBOARD-VERIFICATION.md for the exact limitation and what would unblock it.
Private control-room stills. **Boss only** - this view is absent from the worker view entirely, per docs/DASHBOARD_AND_SECURITY_DECISIONS.md line 49.

cards.title: Control room - freshness audit
Why these are stale
cards.content: The control-room tiles that read months old are the ones written by the **periodic / security loop** (`script.control_room_snapshot_loop`), which is what refreshes `latest_control_room_periodic_*` and `latest_control_room_security_*`. The event-driven tiles (open, presence, intrusion) are current, so the cameras themselves are fine - the recovery point is the loop automation, not the camera.
